candidates.summary: the foreign exemption walks the whole last-descendant chain, closed nodes included, on every line, so render time grows with nesting depth times line count
candidates.failure_scenario:
A realm returns ':::details a
' + '>'x40000 + '
' + '
'x200000 + ':::
' (240 KB, under maxMarkdownRenderBytes). The blockquotes close on the first blank line, but Continue still walks all 40000 closed nodes for each of the 200000 blank lines: the page takes 23 s to render against 0.56 s for the same bytes without the opener, quadrupling with each doubling; the 1 MiB cap allows minutes. The same text in a <gno-foreign> body hits the inner instance, which now loads ExtDetails.

Replacing the loop with 'if _, ok := pc.LastOpenedBlock().Node.(*ForeignNode); ok { return parser.Continue | parser.HasChildren }' (a ForeignNode opens with NoChildren, so an open one is always the last opened block): 'D=20000 N=100000 plain=149.8ms details=153.5ms', and 'go test -run ^Test[^Z] ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown' reads ok, both valid_foreign_colons goldens included.

candidates.summary: the exemption trusts ForeignNode.Closed, which stays false when a blockquote or list closes the foreign, so the details' own ':::' closer is taken as text and the rest of the page folds into the block
candidates.failure_scenario:
':::details A
> <gno-foreign>
> text

:::

footer
': the blank line closes the blockquote and with it the unclosed foreign, through foreignParser.Close, which never sets Closed. On the ':::' line Continue still finds the ForeignNode on the chain, so ':::' renders as a literal paragraph and 'footer' (a realm's footer, its tx links) sits inside the collapsed details. Same output for '- <gno-foreign>
  text

:::' in a list, where the foreign is still open when the list closes on the ':::' line itself. Before 87aa65612 all three shapes close the details and render footer outside.
